patch_description: Structural redesign around a single causal core: a constant-velocity Kalman filter that exposes BOTH its level and slope estimates, eliminating the multi-pass pipeline (Savitzky-Golay → window average → median snap → trend-lock) that over-smoothed and drove lag_error to 0.46, avg_error to 0.56, and correlation down to 0.74. The new architecture: (1) Kalman level+slope states give noise-reduced, near-zero-lag output directly; (2) a vectorized iteratively-reweighted (IRLS, Huber) Savitzky-Golay polish runs once on the Kalman level (robust to residual outliers, preserves polynomial trends); (3) a predictive slope-extrapolation blend in high-NIS regimes adds responsiveness at genuine turning points (fixes lag without adding false reversals); (4) a statistically-gated reversal hysteresis on output diffs only rejects sign flips insignificant w.r.t. local MAD of diffs — one final, principled stage instead of the stacked snap stages. Overall the data flow goes from 5 cascaded smoothers (each adding lag/distortion) to 2 smoothing operations plus adaptive prediction, restoring correlation (0.93 in the top prior programs) and accuracy while keeping slope_changes/false_reversals low.
